<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48:8">Gen. R. s. 48</cite> <he>בארבע … טולא ק׳ וכ׳</he> at four hours of the day the shade is cool, and the sun hot.
<cite ref="Shabbat 53a:11">Sabb. 53ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>חמרא … ק׳ ליה</he> the ass feels cold even at the solstice of Tammuz.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 24b:9">B. Bath. 24ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ולא ק׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H01179"><he>חַמִּים</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 25:25">Targ. Prov. XXV, 25</cite>.—
<cite ref="Niddah 36b:75">Nidd. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>עיילוה … אפקוה מק׳</he> they got him hot to relieve him from chills; <he>עיילוה בק׳ וכ׳</he> they got him cold to relieve him from fever.
Ab. Zar. 28ᵃ מק׳ ק׳ דחיטי from eating very cold wheat dishes; a. e.—Esp. קרירי (מיא) cold water.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 28b:4">Ib.ᵇ</cite> <he>לא ק׳ וכ׳</he> neither cold nor hot, but tepid.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 47:4">Gen. R. s. 47</cite> <he>לא תמלי … קריר וכ׳</he> fill not my spirit with too much pleasure (awaken not in me too high aspirations), Oh that thou wouldst not withdraw from me the present grant!; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 82:6">Yalk. ib. 82</cite>.
